title: Building a Co offending Network: A Social Network of Crime  #datascience #ai #analysis #innovation
description:
Organisations across domains collect vast relational data but struggle to extract meaningful patterns and generate professional intelligence reports from complex networks. Traditional approaches require weeks of manual analysis, miss critical relationships, and produce inconsistent results. The technical challenge lies in combining graph analytics with AI systems that provide reliable, explainable outputs suitable for high-stakes decision-making.

This masterclass addresses the implementation gap: while organisations recognise the potential of Knowledge Graphs + LLMs, they lack practical guidance for building reliable systems that handle real-world data complexity and produce professional-quality analysis.

Why This Matters: Attendees will learn a complete technical methodology that applies beyond criminal networks to fraud detection, supply chain analysis, cybersecurity, and any domain requiring relationship analysis at scale. The techniques covered—graph data science, agentic AI coordination, systematic prompt engineering, and quality evaluation—represent reusable patterns for building explainable AI systems in critical applications.

Technical Approach and Hands-On Learning

Phase 1: Graph-Powered Network Analysis

Transform raw relational data into meaningful co-occurrence networks using association strength calculations
Apply community detection (Louvain) and centrality measures (PageRank, Betweenness) with practical implementation examples
Extract structured intelligence from graph analysis for AI processing

Phase 2: Agentic AI Implementation

Build LangGraph workflows with parallel agent coordination
Implement systematic prompt engineering techniques with measurable quality improvements
Design LLMs-as-judge evaluation systems with bias mitigation protocols
Generate professional HTML reports through coordinated AI agents
Demonstrated Impact: Participants will implement a complete pipeline that processes complex relational data and generates comprehensive analysis reports. The methodology reduces analysis time from weeks to hours while discovering patterns invisible through manual approaches, with reliability suitable for operational deployment.

Target Audience

Level: Intermediate to Advanced Technical
Background: Experience with graph databases, familiarity with Python, basic understanding of LLMs and network analysis concepts
Role: Data scientists, AI engineers, technical architects, analysts working with complex relational data
What Attendees Will Learn:

Technical Implementation Skills:

Practical graph data science techniques with code examples and algorithmic choices
LangGraph architecture patterns for building reliable multi-agent AI systems
Systematic prompt engineering methodologies with measurable evaluation frameworks
Production considerations including security, privacy, and quality assurance protocols
Hands-On Deliverables:

Working implementation of graph-to-intelligence pipeline using provided datasets
Prompt engineering templates and evaluation frameworks for custom applications
LangGraph coordination patterns adaptable to different analytical domains
Quality assessment methodologies for measuring AI system improvements
Transferable Frameworks:

Complete technical methodology for adapting this approach to fraud networks, supply chains, cybersecurity threats, and other relationship-heavy domains
Production deployment considerations including local vs. cloud LLMs, data anonymization, and human-in-the-loop integration
Participants leave with implemented code, systematic methodologies, and practical experience building knowledge graph-powered AI systems that solve real business problems while maintaining explainability and reliability standards.

Alessandro Negro. Chief Scientist, Graph Aware Ltd

Alessandro Negro is the chief scientist at GraphAware, where he supervises the science and technology area responsible for delivering Hume, a mission-critical analytics platform that leverages knowledge graphs (KGs) at its core. He holds a Ph.D. in computer science.
